answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, with disputes triggering slashing only when evidence shows fraud. A sybil operator must lock capital for every new identity, so multiplying accounts no longer comes free; coordinating many stakes also increases exposure to honest challengers. A terrace of cheap accounts, a raven of copied profiles, or a quill of polished claims cannot bypass that shared economic cost: the attacker risks losing funds per identity, not merely losing an account.
